As a complete outsider, going by the information publicly available on these boards I'm guessing the following:

1) New set is announced. Opinions are asked, mixed feelings are expressed with a general lean towards "hey cool idea, as long as you do it right". Designers are appointed based on criteria that I have no know of.
2) Things kick off smoothly and a first pass of cards is made
3) The design team leader, Ben Peal, suffers from some issues in his personal sphere and is unable to communicate with VEKN for a lengthy period of time as a result
4) PCK takes up the brunt of the work while everyone else sits and waits for Ben to returns.
5) Ben Peal eventually returns and design work is being picked up by the rest of the team. Most of PCK's cards are dismissed as crap and removed from playtesting rounds (and given what they published earlier, this seems to make sense...)
6) PCK gets mad that Ben removes their cards from development and drama ensues.
7) Jeff K (the K in PCK) eventually leaves the design team, swiftly followed by Eric Chiang (the C in PCK) who also gets kicked from the IC /Storyline coordinator in the process.
8) More drama ensues.

// at this point most people, including myself, can sympathize with PCK but feels they should just move on

9) Shit settles and everyone forgets about it.
10) Johannes posts good news about VTES maybe maybe maybe seeing some printed cards again.
11) People rejoice!
12) PCK comes in to poop on the party and reveals their "expansion".
13) People treat their "expansion" as just another thread filled with card ideas.
14) People say that this is not a good idea and the copyright crap is both stupid and not even remotely legal either.
15) People express their generic disinterest and mostly tell them most of the cards are bad and that some might be useful given proper tweaking.
16) PCK, sensing lack of support from the community, gets annoyed and looks to exact revenge on VEKN by invoking their copyright in the stupendous mail in the initial post.
17) More drama ensues.

Now, I don't think it's very gentlemen-like from the chairman to actually post this mail in public, but it does shine a new light on the situation.

ok the last few pages were fun, let's go on  and btw. since we started using the "F" words more frequently, I'm not going to stop myself either

Anyway...

1. I happen to be a free thinker, therefore I will support whoever I choose to and I will reserve the right to change my mind whenever I choose to, thank you very much.

2. What some of you consider "support" is actually me trying to stay objective (it is hard, I admit that), simply because I don't have enough data to choose sides. However, just by following my gut and considering the fact that the VEKN treats secrecy as a tool of convenience (ie. we won't tell because it's a secret - when it can harm us, but we'll disclose private emails whenever that suits our cause) naturally my point of view on this issue is as it is. So - while I openly admit of being sympathetic towards the PCK - this is not a support of what PCK does, this is the lack of support of what the VEKN does. Just so we're clear. If the VEKN ever chooses to stop being selectively secretive, I might actually change my mind.

3. I strongly believe that nobody will sue anybody over anything. This is a fan organization in conflict with other fans developing a fan set, no lawyer with the right mind would give a fuck - the only thing that can happen is somebody recruits the lawyer to the game after listening to the explanations of what VTES and VEKN are (after they stop laughing at this "issue", that is). No potential investor / publisher will give a fuck either, as they can simply ignore everything they don't like (they're investing in the product because they have a target that will buy it, that is the only reason).
Nobody is going to destroy the game, the VEKN etc. What we see is a power play combined with an ego issue, which is even more ironic, since this is not a business, there's no money involved and - I'll say it again - nobody outside of this forum gives a fuck about this anyway.

4. I said it once, I will say it again - the communication between the VEKN and its members is pathetic. The OP is a very good example - the title is the verdict at the same time, and then we get one sentence that graciously allows us to build our own opinion. Apparently somebody's been reading The Sun (or other crap newspapers in your country) too much...

5. Ignorance + fear = hatred. Think about this next time before you post (this is to all the hate speech folks). The truth is that we know shit about what's really going on, because it's a "secret", until it becomes convenient not to make it a secret anymore. I'm not posting because I praise what PCK does, I'm posting because I don't like the direction the VEKN is going. At all.

6. Finally, my favourite part - banning people from the VEKN and the tournaments. Really? I mean seriously - do you really want to go there? Let's think about this for a moment, shall we?
What is your authority to ban anyone? On what basis? Who gave you the right to forbid people playing the game they love and have been playing for more than 10 years? How are you planning to execute that? Penalize those guys who allowed the banned people to attend the tournament? Any other bright ideas?

Let's go further - ban me, just for the fun of it. After the players in my country stop laughing their asses off, they will show you the middle finger, simple as that. You really have to face the fact that you have close to no authority outside of this forum and the majority of the global playerbase doesn't even come here. They simply don't care - all they want is to play the game they love, with their friends, for as long as it is still possible. So I wouldn't really go into the legitimacy and authority talks if I were you. Additionally, as it was mentioned in this topic, this forum is getting so bad (mostly because of constant battles and petty games that help absolutely noone) that people are reluctant to recommend it to other players in their playgroups. Think about that during your next power struggle.

So the only nuisance left in the banning issue is the EC, since if I'm banned, I can't attend it. If you banned PCK last year, I would still welcome them to the EC in Warsaw, because in the end it is the organizer's decision. I don't think that the guys from Hungary will be extremely happy that you forbid certain players to attend their tournament and spend money on games / hotels / food / partying and having awesome time.

So to sum it up...
I don't give a flying fuck if you like me, agree with me and what not. All I care about is the future of the game I've devoted 16 years of my life to. The fact that group A can't talk with group B is not my problem. Therefore, I want you to stay the fuck away with your drama. Keep it to yourselves and while you're at it - do your job.

This game will not die because of PCK or VEKN. This game dies when the community dies. Sadly, I have the impression that this will be the only "success" we will see in the near future.

Messages.Author: echiang
Messages.Body:
We readily acknowledge that Hasbro (formerly Wizards of the Coast) and CCP (formerly White Wolf) have relevant copyrights. We are not trying to claim any of their intellectual property. We stated this in the Guardians of the Faith set release announcement. Our focus is on our creative interpretation of the source material. The V:EKN is also free to come up with their own creative interpretation of the source material as well. The issue is whether theirs just happens to be substantially similar to ours.

Back in April, we asked the V:EKN to not use any of our cards without our explicit permission. They never asked for our permission. We did not grant explicit permission other than the six storyline cards. Here's a simple question for the V:EKN now:

Johannes, from April 2012 to September 2012, did the V:EKN use any of our "original ideas" without our explicit permission?

If the answer to the above question is “No,” then the whole situation is moot. We're only concerned with our work, so if you haven't been using our work, then there's no conflict.

However, your September statement referred to some "minor things" that needed to be corrected. There were also several public posts about Guardians of the Faith by playtesters which alluded to numerous similarities to the V:EKN set. We have been quite transparent about the contents of our set, making it available to V:EKN affiliates and some members of the V:EKN Inner Circle. The V:EKN, understandably, has been much more opaque about their set. As a result, we don't know exactly what they've been playtesting or what they plan to publish.

If the answer to the above question is “Yes,” then the V:EKN has been using our "original ideas" even after we asked them not to. As such, I think it would be logical for us to be wary about further assurances from the V:EKN, especially given the information asymmetry.

As others have noted, if the V:EKN was not using our work then our cease and desist letter is irrelevant. It would be a complete non-issue. So the fact that Johannes has made it such a big deal appears to legitimize our concerns about whether the V:EKN has been or is still using our work.

We have repeatedly tried to communicate with the V:EKN and the Inner Circle:

- Before Jeff's whistleblower post in February, there were multiple attempts to communicate with Johannes but he was repeatedly non-responsive.

- Before Carl and Eric's resignation in April, there were multiple attempts to communicate with Johannes but he was repeatedly non-responsive.

- Since April we tried other avenues of communication to no avail. Not once did the V:EKN try to initiate a conversation with us during this period to talk about the possible use of our cards.

- In August, we offered the V:EKN the opportunity to sanction our set. About a month later, we still have not received an official response.

Throughout our numerous attempts to communicate with Johannes and the Inner Circle, the two most common results have been either no response at all or a knee-jerk reaction, sometimes in public, sometimes in private.

IMO, this is much ado about nothing.

PCK has to:

1) Have created non-derivative content, not described in print and/or already protected by copyright/patent held by other entities. Since so many cards are based on existing WoD canon, the subset for point #1 is small.

2) Have not received constructive design input from any second party who might also therefore have ownership rights, and not have duplicated or derived functions from cards proposed on this board to which others might have as much copyright claim as they do.

3) Have not relinquished rights by voluntarily issuing playtest files which included "Confidential Property of VEKN." This seems a high hurdle in my mind, especially if VEKN can produce documentation showing an internal design team approval of the PDF including this language.

4) Be able to specifically demonstrate that a card from Danse Macabre is derivative from some original content to which they could actually claim right. Since VEKN has already stated they will excise that small fraction of cards that don't have directly attributable WoD canon references and.or can be traced to other developers, this should eliminate any problems.

5) Have a standing copyright application in the public domain to initiate legal action. I could find nothing in the public record suggesting an application exists and it seems a huge mistake to even apply for US copyright. The huge amount of derivative content could open PCK to legal action from existing copyright holders, making the attempt backfire horribly.

6) Have funds available to pursue litigation against VEKN, risking countersuit for recovery of the defendant's legal costs. Even if all the stars for Points #1-#5 align, the gut-check associated with Point #6 is a likely roadblock.

Here is where I put my money where my mouth is. If a legal suit does result, I am willing to provide funds for legal consultation to support VEKN's defense (assuming that a personal review of available records for a defense case meets a minimum standard).

I might even sell my extensive collection of VTES original art with all proceeds funding VEKN defense. The irony of Eric buying art to fund the opposition's defense would not be lost on me
